harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a Python-based inventory web app on node2 and node3 (systemd service inventory-app, listening on 0.0.0.0:8080, serving /inventory and /healthz JSON), and configured nginx on node1 as an HTTP load balancer on port 80 (upstream round-robin across 10.100.79.11:8080 and 10.100.79.12:8080). Verified even traffic distribution across both backends. Completed the mandatory sequential restart protocol on all three nodes (one at a time), confirming changed boot_id and full service/LB recovery after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected all three nodes' OS/tooling baseline (Ubuntu 24.04, root access, python3 present)
Installed nginx on node1 via apt
Wrote /opt/inventory-app/app.py (stdlib http.server) on node2 and node3, serving JSON inventory data with host identity
Created and enabled systemd unit inventory-app.service on node2 and node3 (Restart=always, PORT=8080)
Verified each backend responds correctly on its own $NODE_IP:8080/inventory
Configured /etc/nginx/sites-available/inventory-lb on node1 with upstream inventory_backend (node2, node3) and enabled it as default site on port 80
Reloaded/enabled nginx on node1 and validated config with nginx -t
Verified load balancing with repeated curl loops against node1:80/inventory showing even 10/10 split across node2/node3
Captured baseline boot_id, uptime, service status, and app response on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via `reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified nginx active and LB round-robin restored
Restarted node2 via `reboot` while node1+node3 served traffic, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified inventory-app active and rejoined LB rotation (5/5 split)
Restarted node3 via `reboot` while node1+node2 served traffic, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, verified inventory-app active and rejoined LB rotation (5/5 split)

evidence.summary: inventory-app.service enabled+active on node2, python3 listening on 0.0.0.0:8080, /inventory returns host=node2 JSON payload
inventory-app.service enabled+active on node3, python3 listening on 0.0.0.0:8080, /inventory returns host=node3 JSON payload

evidence.requirement: node1 nginx load-balances port 80 across both backends
evidence.summary: nginx config validated (nginx -t OK), service active+listening on 0.0.0.0:80, 20-request sample shows exact 10/10 split between node2 and node3 via upstream round-robin
Captured boot_id 63f96994... , nginx active, LB serving inventory before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement + changed boot identity + recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before disconnect, node unreachable during reboot, reconnected with new boot_id c14f3a3b... (uptime 20:17:05), nginx active and LB round-robin verified (7/3 split, both backends reachable)
Captured boot_id 96c08b66..., inventory-app active, /inventory responding before restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement + changed boot identity + recovery + LB rejoin
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; LB continued serving via node3 during outage; node2 unreachable then reconnected with new boot_id b6b56047... (uptime 20:17:16); inventory-app active and responding; LB shows node2 back in rotation with 5/5 split
Captured boot_id 8d1d94e2..., inventory-app active, /inventory responding before restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement + changed boot identity + recovery + LB rejoin
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; LB continued serving via node2 during outage; node3 unreachable then reconnected with new boot_id 651514b0... (uptime 20:17:27); inventory-app active and responding; final LB check shows full 5/5 even distribution across both backends
